column1: # srf-components.tsv -- what each row of the SRF status spreadsheet MEANS in the bundle.
# copy you pass with --sheet) says WHICH STATUS each row has; this file says which npm packages and
# which other files belong to that row. Rows are matched on the "Software" column, ignoring case and
#   software (as in the sheet) <TAB> npm packages (space-separated) <TAB> other artifacts (space-separated)
#   raw:<path>/      every file under the full bundle's raw/<path>/   (Node, VS Code, uv, Cypress, ...)
#   vsix:<id>        that VS Code extension's .vsix file(s)
#   media:<text>     comes from the RHEL media, not from any bundle (listed in the bundle notes; "-" reads as a space)
#   with:<row>       ships inside another row's file (npm inside the Node.js tarball)
# Every npm package the example stack declares (stack/frontend/package.json, and pnpm/only-allow
# in stack/package-managers) must belong to exactly one row; the planner refuses to build otherwise.
VS Code ext: Angular Language Service
VS Code ext: Python / Pylance / Python Debugger / Python Environments
